composition_start_note: Counted on 14 Dec 2023, once the Port Waikato by-election result had flowed through (Nancy Lu sworn in from National's list); this matches the 123-seat House.

members.notes: Suspended by Te Pāti Māori 23 Oct 2025 and expelled 10 Nov 2025. Wikipedia's 54th Parliament changes table records her return to the party on 5 Dec 2025 (after she sought a High Court injunction, filed 4 Dec 2025); her own article says the High Court ruled the expulsion unlawful on 10 Mar 2026. Sources therefore differ on when she was formally reinstated. She left on 11 May 2026 to found the Te Tai Tokerau Party.

members.notes: Expelled from Te Pāti Māori 10 Nov 2025; independent thereafter. Announced (21 Mar 2026) he would contest Te Tai Tonga as an independent in 2026.

changes.description: 2023 Port Waikato by-election (delayed after ACT candidate Neil Christensen died during the campaign): National list MP Andrew Bayly won the seat (majority 11,432 over NZ First's Casey Costello), creating a third overhang seat (123 seats).
2023-12-05: Andrew Little (labour, List) – Resigned to allow a newer Labour MP into parliament → replaced by Camilla Belich (labour) on 2023-12-06 [List]
2023-12-13: Andrew Bayly (national, List) – Elected to electorate seat → list place filled by Nancy Lu (2023-12-14)
2024-01-18: Golriz Ghahraman (green, List) – Resigned due to shop-lifting allegations → replaced by Celia Wade-Brown (green) on 2024-01-19 [List]
2024-01-28: Rino Tirikatene (labour, List) – Resigned after losing Te Tai Tonga in 2023 election → replaced by Tracey McLellan (labour) on 2024-01-29 [List]
2024-02-06: Kelvin Davis (labour, List) – Resigned after losing Te Tai Tokerau in 2023 election → replaced by Shanan Halbert (labour) on 2024-02-07 [List]
2024-02-21: Efeso Collins (green, List) – Died → replaced by Lawrence Xu-Nan (green) on 2024-03-06 [List]
2024-03-22: Grant Robertson (labour, List) – Resigned to take up the role of Vice-Chancellor of the University of Otago → replaced by Glen Bennett (labour) on 2024-03-25 [List]
2024-05-05: James Shaw (green, List) – Resigned to take up governance and advisory roles in the climate sector → replaced by Francisco Hernandez (green) on 2024-05-06 [List]
2024-07-08: Darleen Tana (green, List) – Resigned from the Green Party due to allegations of migrant exploitation → now independent

2024-10-22: Darleen Tana (independent, List) – Expelled from Parliament under the Electoral (Integrity) Amendment Act 2018 → replaced by Benjamin Doyle (green) on 2024-10-22 [Green gain;Independent loss]
2025-05-12: David Parker (labour, List) – Resigned → replaced by Vanushi Walters (labour) on 2025-05-12 [List]
2025-06-26: Takutai Tarsh Kemp (te-pati-maori, Tāmaki Makaurau) – Died → replaced by Oriini Kaipara (te-pati-maori) on 2025-09-06 [Te Pāti Māori hold(By-election)]
2025-06-27: Tanya Unkovich (nz-first, List) – Resigned → replaced by David Wilson (nz-first) on 2025-06-30 [List]
2025-10-03: Benjamin Doyle (green, List) – Resigned → replaced by Mike Davidson (green) on 2025-10-06 [List]
2025-11-10: Tākuta Ferris (te-pati-maori, Te Tai Tonga) – Expelled from Te Pāti Māori → now independent
2025-11-10: Mariameno Kapa-Kingi (te-pati-maori, Te Tai Tokerau) – Expelled from Te Pāti Māori → now independent
2025-12-05: Mariameno Kapa-Kingi (independent, Te Tai Tokerau) – Allowed to return to Te Pāti Māori via Court trial → now te-pati-maori
2026-02-06: Adrian Rurawhe (labour, List) – Resigned → replaced by Georgie Dansey (labour) on 2026-02-09 [List]
2026-03-16: Peeni Henare (labour, List) – Resigned → replaced by Dan Rosewarne (labour) on 2026-03-16 [List]

2026-05-11: Mariameno Kapa-Kingi (te-pati-maori, Te Tai Tokerau) – Left Te Pāti Māori and announced the new Te Tai Tokerau Party (registered Aug 2026); sat as an independent MP for the rest of the term → now independent

2026-05-14: Judith Collins (national, Papakura) – Resigned to take up role as the President of the New Zealand Law Commission → seat left vacant (no by-election required within 6 months of a general election)
